title: IsLocallyFinite — finite faces and finite cofaces
body_html:
IsLocallyFinite

A Prop mixin, independent of the AbstractCellComplex — dimension function on a face poset data, asserting that each cell has only finitely many faces and lies in only finitely many cells' closures:

Signature

lean class IsLocallyFinite (X : Type*) [PartialOrder X] : Prop where finite_faces : ∀ E : X, Set.Finite {F : X | F ≤ E} finite_cofaces : ∀ E : X, Set.Finite {F : X | E ≤ F}

  • finite_faces: the down-set at each cell $E$ is finite (closure of $E$ meets finitely many cells).
  • finite_cofaces: the up-set at each cell $E$ is finite ($E$ lies in the closure of finitely many cells).

Why both

Both conditions together formalise "each point has a neighbourhood meeting only finitely many cells" for a regular CW complex. In the abstract poset setting, the two are independent — neither implies the other without further structure — but for a regular CW complex the geometric "locally finite" assumption delivers both at once. Bundling them in a single Prop class matches the CW-intuition and keeps downstream lemmas single-parameter.

Design choice: Prop mixin, not part of AbstractCellComplex

Finiteness is split out because the abstract poset / dimension structure is meaningful without it (and many lemmas — e.g. the star-topology basis, iota order-embedding — do not need finiteness). Downstream files pick up the finiteness typeclass only when the sum ∑_E V_E or a Finset argument is unavoidable.
